diagram_math_checks.evidence: Definition lines 34–38 defines E_t subset V_(t-1) x V_t for 2<=t<=T. The example has T=3 and disjoint labeled columns V1={a,b}, V2={c,d}, V3={e,f}; arrows are exactly E2={(a,c),(a,d),(b,d)} and E3={(c,e),(d,e),(d,f)}. All six arrows point to the next layer; no within-layer, backward, skipped-layer or unlisted edge is drawn.

Definition lines 35–39 requires positive edge weights and nonnegative endpoint maps. Diagram sets w2(a,c)=2,w3(c,e)=3 and the remaining four allowed edge weights to 1. Alpha is displayed only on V1 (a=1,b=0), beta only on V3 (e=1,f=0). Zero endpoint values disable endpoint use without deleting the allowed incident edge.

Definition lines 41–46 gives the score alpha(v1) times edge-weight product times beta(vT). The bold route (a,c,e) uses E2(a,c),E3(c,e) and positive endpoints, with score 1*2*3*1=6. Route (a,d,e) uses the two diagonal weight-1 edges and has score 1*1*1*1=1. There are no other admissible paths: starts at b and ends at f fail the endpoint condition. Both c and d admit prefixes from a, satisfying the reachability definition at lines 48–52.

The unchanged Definition remains complete without the figure. Added prose explicitly restricts the example to T=3 and preserves the original T=0 empty path and T=1 empty-product conventions; no proof depends on the picture.
